documents.title: Board Meeting Intimation for Consideration Of Audited Financial Results For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Disclosure Of Information Under Regulation 30 Of SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015, Reply To Clarification Sought On Spurt In Volume Of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited Shares
Clarification sought from Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported stellar operational and financial performance for Q4 and FY26, achieving a highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and record production across multiple value-added products. The company maintained a comfortable debt-to-equity ratio and announced a total dividend of INR 62 per share for the year, alongside planning significant capex projects including Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS and retail outlets. Management emphasized its focus on operational efficiency, flexible crude sourcing, and capital discipline despite external logistical and price volatility. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited held its Q4 FY25 earnings conference call on May 2, 2025, discussing its physical and financial performance, capital expenditures, and project updates. Management reported robust operational metrics including a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT and a lower fuel and loss rate, despite lower gross refining margins (GRMs) year-over-year due to industry-wide cracks.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that motor spirit (MS) in the southern market has a shortfall where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern market's MS demand is projected to grow around 4%-5% while HSD is projected at a 3% growth forecast.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has approved all clearances for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project, which has a budget of INR 1,600 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL has taken 300 licenses for retail outlets, and commissioning will start in FY27.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet project capex is INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: Normal capex is assumed to be another INR 500 crores every year.
capex_expansion.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: The company spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: Maintenance CAPEX is expected to remain in the Rs. 200-250 crore range for the next year.
capex_expansion.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the CBR project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil respectively.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CBR update, in the last year we revised the capital cost as well as the capital structure. The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: The new refinery capital cost is approximately Rs. 36,000 Crore with 9 million metric ton capacity and a petrochemical intensity of 6% for polypropylene.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

margins_costs.claim: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for the quarter was $10.3 per barrel.
Foreign exchange loss for the quarter was approximately INR 200 crores.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,.

margins_costs.claim: Foreign exchange loss for the whole year was around INR 350 crores.
margins_costs.quote: And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: The full year GRM for 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: The inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: The fuel and loss for the year as a whole has come down to 8.51%.
margins_costs.quote: I must place it that if you remember our Energy Indexes and our Fuel and Loss Indexes were quite high 2-3 years back and we went to a roadmap where we said on a sustained basis, we will bring it down to very efficient levels and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

margins_costs.claim: The annual average discount for opportunity crude in FY24-25 was around $1.5-$2 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: Last year, that is the Financial Year’24-25, the average was around $1.5-$2. But it has gone to a high of $3-$4 and to a low of less than $1 also.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved the highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, which is equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: In Q4 FY26, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: Hexane capacity has been doubled from 30 to 60.
orders_capacity.quote: It was 30, now the capacity is 60.

orders_capacity.claim: The new LOBS unit will add a fresh capacity of 250,000 KTPA in Group 2 and Group 3.
orders_capacity.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.18 on a gross level.
capital_allocation.quote: Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: On a gross basis, borrowings are INR 1,900 crores, and on a net basis, it is INR 973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: If net borrowing is considered, the debt ratio is 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR 62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: Capex during the current year was INR 856 crores compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of face value for the current year.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: Total absolute debt as on March 31, 2025, stands at Rs. 3,100 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: Net worth is reported at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management stated that uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects to commission retail outlets in the financial year 2026-2027.
management_commitments.quote: And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that refinery crude unit 1 which caters to lubes will go into maintenance around August or September 2025.
management_commitments.quote: In 2025, our refinery crude unit 1 which caters to lubes will go into maintenance around August, September.

management_commitments.claim: Management expects normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
